newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Optus says has other plans for local calls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Optus says has other plans for local calls.

text.p: Optus Communications Pty Ltd said on Wednesday it had plans to provide a full coverage of its services to Australian customers and would use alternatives to its associate Optus Vision for the local telephone call market.

Optus Vision, which is 46.5 percent owned by Optus Communications, is currently rolling out its cable network to 2.5 million homes or 40 percent of Australian households. The network carries local telephony services for the Optus group.
Optus has invested about A$605 million in Optus Vision, which is currently subject to litigation by one of its shareholders Seven Network Ltd.
"It has never been Optus Vision's intention to cable up to 100 percent of Australia's population," Optus Communications chief operating officer Phil Jacobs told reporters.

"It has been our intention as Optus Communications to offer our services to a wide a customer base as possible and we have from the very beginning looked at a multiple strategy to get to those customers," Jacobs said.

Optus Communications would not comment on the ligitation involving Optus Vision or its local telephney service, which was launched last year with much fanfare as its broke the government owned Telstra Corp's monopoly on the local A$5 billion market.

"With those 50 to 60 percent of the homes that we don't have connections to we are looking at a variety of services, from reselling Telstra services, to the development of alternative telephony capabilities through our wireless systems,...or even the capability that is beginning to emerge with our satellite operations," Jacobs said.

If Optus Vision loses the legal battle with Seven, Optus Communications may be foreced to sell its Vision stake at a discount to Seven. The ligitation has already delayed the planned float of Optus Communications.
Optus earlier reported a net profit of A$58.9 million for the six months ended December 31, 1996, compared with A$7.1 million a year earlier.
Optus is owned 25 percent by Mayne Nickless Ltd and 24.5 percent each by Cable and Wireless Plc of the United Kingdom and U.S. carrier BellSouth Corp Inc.
The remainder is owned by Australian institutions.
